exercises.question: You're adding the definite article הַ to סֵפֶר (book). What happens?

options.text: הַסֵּפֶר — the ס doubles
הַסֵפֶר — nothing changes
הֵסֵפֶר — the vowel lengthens

exercises.explanation: When הַ is added, the first letter of the noun doubles (Dagesh Forte). Since ס can take a dagesh, we get הַסֵּפֶר.

exercises.question: You're adding the definite article הַ to עָם (nation). What happens?

options.text: הַעָּם — the ע doubles
הָעָם — the vowel under ה lengthens
הַעָם — nothing changes

exercises.explanation: ע is a guttural and cannot double. Instead, the patach under הַ lengthens to qamets: הָעָם.

exercises.question: You're combining מִן with בַּיִת (house). What happens?

options.text: מִנְבַּיִת — the נ stays
מִבַּיִת — the נ assimilates, בּ doubles and hardens
מֵבַיִת — the vowel lengthens

exercises.explanation: The נ assimilates into the ב, which doubles (Dagesh Forte Compensative). Since ב is a BeGaD KePhaT letter, the dagesh also hardens it: מִבַּיִת (mib-bayit).

exercises.question: You're combining מִן with רֹאשׁ (head). What happens?

options.text: מִרֹּאשׁ — the ר doubles
מֵרֹאשׁ — the vowel lengthens because ר can't double
מִנְרֹאשׁ — the נ stays

exercises.explanation: The נ should assimilate and cause ר to double, but ר refuses to double. Instead, the chirik lengthens to tsere: מֵרֹאשׁ.

exercises.question: You're combining מִן with גַּן (garden). What happens?

options.text: מִגַּן — the נ assimilates, גּ doubles and hardens
מֵגַן — the vowel lengthens
מִנְגַּן — the נ stays

exercises.explanation: The נ assimilates into the ג, which doubles (Dagesh Forte). Since ג is a BeGaD KePhaT letter, the dagesh also hardens it from 'gh' to 'g': מִגַּן (mig-gan).

exercises.instruction: Why doesn't this letter have a dagesh?
exercises.question: Why does the ב in לֵבָב (heart) NOT have a dagesh?

options.text: ב never takes a dagesh
Both בs follow vowels — they close syllables, not begin them
It's a guttural letter

exercises.explanation: Dagesh Lene only appears when a BeGaD KePhaT letter begins a syllable with no vowel before it. Both בs in לֵבָב follow vowels (tsere and qamets), so neither gets a dagesh.

exercises.instruction: Why doesn't this letter have a dagesh?
exercises.question: Why does the פ in אֶלֶף (thousand) NOT have a dagesh?

options.text: The פ follows a vowel (segol under ל)
פ never takes a dagesh at the end of a word
It's not a BeGaD KePhaT letter

exercises.explanation: The פ follows the segol under ל, so there's a vowel immediately before it. Dagesh Lene only appears when there's NO vowel before the letter.

exercises.instruction: Why doesn't this letter have a dagesh?
exercises.question: Why does the כ in מַלְאָךְ (angel) NOT have a dagesh?

options.text: The כ begins the syllable after a sheva
The כ follows a vowel (qamets under א)
כ at the end of a word never takes a dagesh

exercises.explanation: The כ follows the qamets under א. Since a vowel comes immediately before it, it cannot have Dagesh Lene.

exercises.instruction: Tap every letter that contains a dagesh
exercises.question: Which letters have a dagesh?
exercises.explanation: וַ has a dagesh in the ו, דּ has Dagesh Lene (begins syllable after sheva), בּ has Dagesh Forte (Pi'el doubling).

exercises.instruction: Tap every letter that contains a dagesh
exercises.question: Which letters have a dagesh?
exercises.explanation: First כּ (Dagesh Forte after connecting hyphen), second כּ (Dagesh Lene — begins word), דּ (Dagesh Lene — begins syllable after sheva).

exercises.instruction: Tap every letter that contains a dagesh
exercises.question: Which letters have a dagesh?
exercises.hebrewText: בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם
exercises.explanation: בּ (Dagesh Lene — begins the word), תּ (Dagesh Forte — doubled). Note: הָעוֹלָם has no dagesh — the ע is a guttural so the vowel lengthened instead.

exercises.question: In the word מִתּוֹךְ, the תּ has a dagesh. Work through the logic: Is there a vowel before the תּ?

options.text: Yes — chirik under מ comes before תּ, so this is Dagesh Forte (doubled)
No — the תּ begins the word, so this is Dagesh Lene
No — sheva comes before it, so this is Dagesh Lene

exercises.explanation: The chirik under מ is a full vowel that comes immediately before תּ. When a vowel precedes a dagesh, it's Dagesh Forte. This is from מִן + תּוֹךְ — the נ assimilated and תּ doubled.

exercises.question: In the word בְּרֵאשִׁית, the בּ has a dagesh. Is there a vowel before the בּ?

options.text: Yes — so this is Dagesh Forte
No — the בּ begins the word, so this is Dagesh Lene (hardened)
No — but it's still Dagesh Forte because it's doubled

exercises.explanation: Nothing comes before בּ — it's the first letter of the word. With no vowel before it and being a BeGaD KePhaT letter, this is Dagesh Lene, hardening the 'v' to 'b'.

exercises.question: The word כַּפְתּוֹר has TWO dageshim. What type is each?

options.text: כּ is Dagesh Lene (begins word), תּ is Dagesh Lene (after sheva)
Both are Dagesh Forte (both doubled)
כּ is Dagesh Forte, תּ is Dagesh Lene

exercises.explanation: כּ begins the word with no vowel before it — Dagesh Lene. תּ comes after the sheva under פ (sheva is not a full vowel), so it also has Dagesh Lene.

exercises.question: The word הִנֵּה has a dagesh in the נּ. What type and why?

options.text: Dagesh Lene — נ is a BeGaD KePhaT letter
Dagesh Forte — the נ is doubled (follows the chirik under ה)
Neither — this is just a printing variation

exercises.explanation: נ is NOT a BeGaD KePhaT letter, so it can only have Dagesh Forte. The dagesh shows the נ is doubled. This follows the chirik under ה.

exercises.instruction: Break down what happened in this word
exercises.explanation: מִן + suffix = מִמֶּנּוּ. The נ of מִן assimilated into the following מ, which doubled. Then the pronoun suffix was added. The מּ has Dagesh Forte Compensative.

exercises.instruction: Break down what happened in this word
exercises.explanation: מִן + פָּנִים = מִפְּנֵי. The נ assimilated into the פ, which doubled (Dagesh Forte). Since פ is BeGaD KePhaT, it also hardened from 'f' to 'p'.

exercises.instruction: Break down what happened in this word
exercises.explanation: מִן + הַר = מֵהַר. The נ should cause doubling, but ה is a guttural and can't double. The chirik lengthened to tsere to compensate.

exercises.instruction: Break down what happened in this word
exercises.explanation: מִן + עַל = מֵעַל. The נ should cause ע to double, but ע is a guttural. The chirik lengthened to tsere instead.

exercises.instruction: Match each מִן combination to its result

exercises.statement: If a BeGaD KePhaT letter has Dagesh Forte, it still performs the Lene function (hardening) as well.
exercises.explanation: True. When a BeGaD KePhaT letter has Dagesh Forte, the dagesh does double duty — it doubles the letter AND hardens the sound.

exercises.statement: A sheva counts as a vowel when determining Dagesh Lene.
exercises.explanation: False. Sheva (whether silent or vocal) does not count as a full vowel. A BeGaD KePhaT letter following a sheva can have Dagesh Lene.

exercises.statement: The word שִׁמְשׁוֹן (Samson) contains a Dagesh Forte.
exercises.explanation: False. The שׁ at the beginning has Dagesh Lene (begins the word). The מ has no dagesh. There's no Dagesh Forte in this word.

exercises.question: You see the word נָתַתִּי (I gave). The תּ in the middle has a dagesh. What type?

options.text: Dagesh Lene — it's a BeGaD KePhaT letter beginning a syllable
Dagesh Forte — it follows a vowel (patach under ת) and is doubled
Neither — this is a scribal error

exercises.explanation: The תּ follows the patach under the first ת. A vowel before a dagesh = Dagesh Forte. The letter is doubled: na-TAT-ti.

exercises.question: In קִדַּשְׁתָּנוּ (You sanctified us), the דּ has a dagesh. Why?

options.text: Dagesh Lene — ד begins a syllable
Dagesh Forte Compensative — a letter assimilated
Dagesh Forte Characteristic — this is a Pi'el verb

exercises.explanation: קִדַּשְׁתָּנוּ is from the root ק-ד-שׁ in the Pi'el pattern. In Pi'el, the middle root letter (ד) doubles. This is Dagesh Forte Characteristic.
